text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash involve the palms of the hands and soles of the feet, and are there any blistering lesions or conjunctivitis present? I also need to know if the mother has any active skin lesions or sores.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules. I also have Rash with an erythematous base, Rash over the trunk and extremities, Sparing of the palms and soles.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the maternal history of untreated gonorrhea and the presence of pustules, I suspect a congenital infection. REQUEST TEST: Gram_stain_of_pustule_exudate

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the rash spares the palms and soles and the Gram stain is normal, this presentation is classic for Erythema Toxicum Neonatorum, a benign, self-limiting condition. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Toxicum Neonatorum
